X1.name: Smart vs Premium vs Health Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: Smart Group (smart features and subscription messaging), Premium Group (design and brand prestige messaging), Health Group (health and low-impact messaging). Each group sees a product description of a differentiated combi-steamer and is asked to indicate willingness to pay a fixed price (e.g., €1,200) and to choose a purchase channel (online, retail).
X1.sample: 300 adult home cooks recruited via an online panel, balanced across the three groups (100 per group).
X1.measure: 1) Willingness to pay (WTP) in euros. 2) Purchase intent (binary: would buy). 3) Channel preference (online vs retail).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Smart Group will show the highest WTP and purchase intent among home cooks, while Premium and Health Groups will show lower WTP and purchase intent.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Premium Group will show the highest WTP and purchase intent, while Smart and Health Groups will show lower WTP and purchase intent.
prediction_by_theory.T3: Health Group will show the highest WTP and purchase intent, while Smart and Premium Groups will show lower WTP and purchase intent.

X1.decision_rule: If the Smart Group's average WTP is at least 20% higher than the Premium Group's and at least 15% higher than the Health Group's, we conclude that smart features drive adoption and recommend developing a differentiated home-cook proposition with smart and subscription capabilities. If the Premium Group's average WTP is at least 20% higher than the Smart Group's and at least 15% higher than the Health Group's, we conclude that design and brand prestige drive adoption and recommend a premium positioning. If the Health Group's average WTP is at least 20% higher than the Smart Group's and at least 15% higher than the Premium Group's, we conclude that health messaging drives adoption and recommend a health-focused proposition. If none of these thresholds are met, we conclude insufficient evidence to favor any theory and recommend no expansion.

final.recommendation: Develop a differentiated home-cook proposition that integrates smart features and a subscription model, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing combi-steamer technology to address home cooks’ demand for convenience and personalized cooking.
final.target_customer: Affluent, tech‑savvy home cooks who value convenience, personalized cooking, and are willing to pay for smart and subscription services.
final.value_proposition: A smart, subscription‑enabled combi‑steamer that learns cooking preferences, delivers recipes, and provides ongoing support, offering a convenient, personalized cooking experience at a premium price point.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Smart vs Premium vs Health Messaging Test (300 participants, 6‑week timeline, €20,000 budget) to measure willingness to pay, purchase intent, and channel preference across the three messaging groups.
final.uncertainty: The test will determine whether smart features, design and brand prestige, or health messaging drive adoption. Current evidence is limited to company assertions and market facts, and no direct consumer survey data is available.
would_change_if: If the Smart Group shows a willingness to pay at least 20% higher than the Premium Group and at least 15% higher than the Health Group, we would shift focus to smart‑feature positioning.
If the Premium Group shows a willingness to pay at least 20% higher than the Smart Group and at least 15% higher than the Health Group, we would shift focus to premium positioning.
If the Health Group shows a willingness to pay at least 20% higher than the Smart Group and at least 15% higher than the Premium Group, we would shift focus to health‑focused positioning.

arguments.name: Smart vs Premium vs Health Messaging Test
arguments.method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: Smart Group (smart features and subscription messaging), Premium Group (design and brand prestige messaging), Health Group (health and low-impact messaging). Each group sees a product description of a differentiated combi-steamer and is asked to indicate willingness to pay a fixed price (e.g., €1,200) and to choose a purchase channel (online, retail).
arguments.sample: 300 adult home cooks recruited via an online panel, balanced across the three groups (100 per group).
arguments.measure: 1) Willingness to pay (WTP) in euros. 2) Purchase intent (binary: would buy). 3) Channel preference (online vs retail).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Smart Group will show the highest WTP and purchase intent among home cooks, while Premium and Health Groups will show lower WTP and purchase intent.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Premium Group will show the highest WTP and purchase intent, while Smart and Health Groups will show lower WTP and purchase intent.
prediction_by_theory.T3: Health Group will show the highest WTP and purchase intent, while Smart and Premium Groups will show lower WTP and purchase intent.

arguments.decision_rule: If the Smart Group's average WTP is at least 20% higher than the Premium Group's and at least 15% higher than the Health Group's, we conclude that smart features drive adoption and recommend developing a differentiated home-cook proposition with smart and subscription capabilities. If the Premium Group's average WTP is at least 20% higher than the Smart Group's and at least 15% higher than the Health Group's, we conclude that design and brand prestige drive adoption and recommend a premium positioning. If the Health Group's average WTP is at least 20% higher than the Smart Group's and at least 15% higher than the Premium Group's, we conclude that health messaging drives adoption and recommend a health-focused proposition. If none of these thresholds are met, we conclude insufficient evidence to favor any theory and recommend no expansion.

result.note: Proposed only. Nothing has been run, and its figures are analyst assumptions.

Competitors do not offer a comparable subscription-based model.

X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are recruited from a panel of home cooks (n=500). Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a subscription-based combi-steamer description emphasizing automation, recurring revenue, and recipe access. Group B receives a premium-priced combi-steamer description emphasizing precision cooking, professional-grade results, and high performance. Both groups see the same product specifications and price point.
X1.sample: 500 home cooks recruited from an online panel, balanced across age, gender, and cooking frequency.
X1.measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7-point Likert scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely) and willingness to pay a recurring subscription fee (EUR 9.99/month).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay the subscription fee than Group B.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay the premium price than Group A.

X1.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent for Group A is at least 1.5 points higher than Group B (i.e., Group A average >= 5.5), proceed with the subscription-based differentiated proposition. If the average purchase intent for Group B is at least 1.5 points higher than Group A (i.e., Group B average >= 5.5), proceed with the premium-priced differentiated proposition. If neither difference meets the threshold, do not expand into either segment.

final.recommendation: Develop a differentiated subscription-based combi-steamer proposition targeting home cooks, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing combi-steamer technology and marketing it as a smart, automated cooking solution with recurring revenue. Conduct a limited pilot to test demand before full rollout.

frame.objective: Determine whether RATIONAL AG should develop a differentiated proposition for home cooks using its commercial combi-steamer technology, or remain focused on professional kitchens, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.
constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.

Any recommendation must be justified by observable data, not assumptions.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated home‑cook proposition (e.g., compact, smart, or subscription‑based combi‑steamer for residential use).
2) Stay focused on professional kitchens (no new home‑cook offering).

4) No expansion (maintain current B2B focus).
5) License the combi‑steamer technology to third‑party manufacturers for residential use.

X1.name: Smart vs Premium Combi-Steamer Test
X1.method: Online survey with simulated purchase intent and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.
X1.sample: 500 adult home cooks recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and region.
X1.measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and WTP (percentage of device price).

prediction_by_theory.T1: At least 30% of respondents will indicate purchase intent for the smart, subscription-based combi-steamer; WTP will be at least 20% of the device price.
prediction_by_theory.T2: At least 25% of respondents will indicate purchase intent for the premium, high-performance combi-steamer; WTP will be at least 30% of the device price.

X1.decision_rule: If the smart-combi-steamer reaches the 30% purchase intent threshold and its WTP is at least 20%, proceed to develop a subscription-based home-cook proposition. If the premium-combi-steamer reaches the 25% purchase intent threshold and its WTP is at least 30%, develop a premium positioning proposition. If neither threshold is met, maintain the current B2B focus.

final.recommendation: Develop a differentiated subscription-based home-cook proposition for the combi-steamer, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing B2B reputation and the identified market potential of 4.8 million customers. The test should focus on purchase intent and willingness-to-pay for a smart, subscription model.
final.target_customer: Home cooks who value convenience, recurring revenue, and smart home integration, particularly those who cook occasionally and seek ongoing value.
final.value_proposition: A subscription-based combi-steamer that automates cooking, delivers recipes, and provides recurring revenue, offering a lower upfront cost and continuous service compared to a premium, one-time purchase.
final.next_action: Run the proposed 12‑week, €20,000 online survey test with 500 home cooks to measure purchase intent and willingness-to-pay for the smart, subscription model.
final.uncertainty: The willingness of home cooks to pay recurring subscription fees and their actual purchase intent remain uncertain. The test will provide data to resolve this uncertainty.
would_change_if: If the test shows purchase intent below 30% or willingness-to-pay below 20% of the device price, the recommendation would shift to maintain the current B2B focus.
If additional evidence shows strong demand for premium, high‑performance features, the recommendation could shift toward a premium positioning proposition.

arguments.method: Online survey with simulated purchase intent and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.
arguments.sample: 500 adult home cooks recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and region.
arguments.measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and WTP (percentage of device price).

prediction_by_theory.T1: At least 30% of respondents will indicate purchase intent for the smart, subscription-based combi-steamer; WTP will be at least 20% of the device price.
prediction_by_theory.T2: At least 25% of respondents will indicate purchase intent for the premium, high-performance combi-steamer; WTP will be at least 30% of the device price.

arguments.decision_rule: If the smart-combi-steamer reaches the 30% purchase intent threshold and its WTP is at least 20%, proceed to develop a subscription-based home-cook proposition. If the premium-combi-steamer reaches the 25% purchase intent threshold and its WTP is at least 30%, develop a premium positioning proposition. If neither threshold is met, maintain the current B2B focus.

frame.objective: Determine whether RATIONAL AG should develop a differentiated proposition for home cooks using its commercial combi-steamer technology, or remain focused on professional kitchens, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.
constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Evidence must demonstrate demand, willingness to pay, or competitive advantage for either home‑cook or professional‑kitchen segments.
Any recommendation must be justified by observable data, not assumptions.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated home‑cook proposition (e.g., compact, smart, or subscription‑based combi‑steamer for residential use).
2) Stay focused on professional kitchens (no new home‑cook offering).
3) Expand into both segments (home and professional) with separate product lines or marketing.
4) No expansion (maintain current B2B focus).
5) License the combi‑steamer technology to third‑party manufacturers for residential use.

T1.claim: Home cooks will purchase a differentiated combi-steamer only if it is marketed as a premium, lifestyle cooking tool that offers superior health benefits (e.g., steam-cooking savings) and design appeal, because they currently view combi-steamers as industrial equipment and prefer established consumer brands.
T1.who_benefits: Health-conscious home cooks willing to pay a premium for convenience and health advantages.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: If RATIONAL frames the product as a modern, stylish appliance that delivers faster, healthier meals, they will shift from generic appliances to a premium offering.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Higher price points and repeat purchases from a niche segment of affluent home cooks.
assumptions: Home cooks perceive steam-cooking as a benefit.
There is a segment willing to pay a premium for design and convenience.
Marketing can differentiate RATIONAL's technology from competitors.
predictions: A survey of home cooks would show at least 30% would consider purchasing a premium combi-steamer at a price 20% above standard models.
Sales would be concentrated among demographics with higher disposable income and interest in culinary gadgets.
T1.first_claim: Home cooks will purchase a differentiated combi-steamer only if it is marketed as a premium, lifestyle cooking tool that offers superior health benefits (e.g., steam-cooking savings) and design appeal, because they currently view combi-steamers as industrial equipment and prefer established consumer brands.

T2.claim: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer primarily because of convenience and time savings, not premium design or health benefits, because they already use multiple appliances and seek solutions that reduce cooking time.
T2.who_benefits: Busy home cooks who value efficiency and time savings in meal preparation.
T2.why_behaviour_changes: If RATIONAL offers a compact, single-appliance solution that cooks multiple dishes simultaneously, home cooks will switch from a collection of separate appliances to a streamlined system.
T2.how_value_is_captured: Higher volume sales through a single product and repeat purchases due to convenience.
assumptions: Home cooks have limited cooking time and prefer one appliance for multiple tasks.
Time savings are a primary purchase driver for home cooks.
RATIONAL can demonstrate measurable time savings in product testing.
predictions: A pilot test of a compact combi-steamer would show at least 40% of participants reducing cooking time by at least 30 minutes per meal.
Purchase intent would be higher among households with children or multiple meals to prepare daily.
T2.first_claim: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer primarily because of convenience and time savings, not premium design or health benefits, because they already use multiple appliances and seek solutions that reduce cooking time.

position.recommendation: Develop a differentiated subscription-based smart combi-steamer proposition for home cooks, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing combi-steamer technology and B2B reputation. The test should validate purchase intent and willingness to pay for a subscription model before scaling.

frame.objective: Determine whether RATIONAL AG should develop a differentiated proposition for home cooks using its commercial combi-steamer technology, or remain focused on professional kitchens, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.
constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Evidence must demonstrate demand, willingness to pay, or competitive advantage for either home‑cook or professional‑kitchen segments.
Any recommendation must be justified by observable data, not assumptions.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated home‑cook proposition (e.g., compact, smart, or subscription‑based combi‑steamer for residential use).
2) Stay focused on professional kitchens (no new home‑cook offering).
3) Expand into both segments (home and professional) with separate product lines or marketing.
4) No expansion (maintain current B2B focus).
5) License the combi‑steamer technology to third‑party manufacturers for residential use.

T1.why_behaviour_changes: Smart home integration and subscription model reduce upfront cost and provide ongoing value, making the appliance attractive to tech-savvy consumers.
T1.how_value_is_captured: RATIONAL captures value through subscription fees and premium pricing for smart features, while also leveraging its existing B2B reputation to build trust.
assumptions: Home cooks are willing to pay a subscription fee for convenience.
Smart home integration is accessible and affordable to residential users.
RATIONAL can adapt its commercial technology to a residential subscription model without significant redesign.
predictions: A test offering a subscription-based smart combi-steamer will generate at least 10% monthly recurring revenue from a sample of 500 home cooks within 12 weeks.
Surveyed participants will rate the device 7/10 or higher on convenience and willingness to pay a monthly fee.

position.recommendation: Develop a differentiated subscription-based combi-steamer for home cooks, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing combi-steamer technology and smart‑home integration capabilities. The subscription model provides recurring revenue and aligns with home‑cook convenience needs.

frame.objective: Determine whether RATIONAL AG should develop a differentiated proposition for home cooks using its commercial combi-steamer technology, or remain focused on professional kitchens, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.
constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Evidence must demonstrate demand, willingness to pay, or competitive advantage for either home‑cook or professional‑kitchen segments.
Any recommendation must be justified by observable data, not assumptions.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated home‑cook proposition (e.g., compact, smart, or subscription‑based combi‑steamer for residential use).
2) Stay focused on professional kitchens (no new home‑cook offering).
3) Expand into both segments (home and professional) with separate product lines or marketing.
4) No expansion (maintain current B2B focus).
5) License the combi‑steamer technology to third‑party manufacturers for residential use.

T1.claim: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if it is marketed as a smart, subscription-based device that automates cooking and delivers recipes, because they value convenience and recurring services.
T1.who_benefits: Home cooks seeking time-saving, automated cooking solutions.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: They would switch from traditional ovens or stovetops to a device that learns their preferences and sends automated recipes, reducing manual effort and decision fatigue.
T1.how_value_is_captured: RATIONAL would capture value through recurring subscription fees for recipe updates, software maintenance, and premium hardware sales, creating a recurring revenue stream.
assumptions: Home cooks are willing to pay a monthly fee for smart cooking automation.
The device can be integrated with existing smart home ecosystems.
Subscription model is feasible without significant hardware redesign.
predictions: In a test offering a subscription-based combi-steamer, at least 30% of surveyed home cooks will sign up within 3 months.
Repeat purchase rate for subscription will be at least 15% within 12 months.
T1.first_claim: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if it is marketed as a smart, subscription-based device that automates cooking and delivers recipes, because they value convenience and recurring services.

T2.claim: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if it is positioned as a premium, high-performance appliance that offers superior cooking performance and durability, because they value professional-quality results and are willing to pay a premium for it.
T2.who_benefits: Home cooks who cook frequently and seek professional-level results.
T2.why_behaviour_changes: They would switch from lower-cost consumer appliances to a device that delivers consistent, high-quality results, reducing the need for multiple cookware items and time spent troubleshooting.
T2.how_value_is_captured: RATIONAL would capture value through premium pricing, limited-edition designs, and brand positioning as a professional-grade appliance, generating higher margins and brand loyalty.
assumptions: Home cooks are willing to pay a premium for performance and durability.
The combi-steamer can be marketed as a professional-grade product without compromising home use.
Marketing can effectively communicate performance advantages.
predictions: In a test offering a premium-combi-steamer, at least 25% of surveyed home cooks will express intent to purchase within 3 months.
Purchase intent will be higher among home cooks who cook multiple meals daily compared to occasional cooks.
T2.first_claim: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if it is positioned as a premium, high-performance appliance that offers superior cooking performance and durability, because they value professional-quality results and are willing to pay a premium for it.

X1.name: Subscription vs Premium Combi-Steamer Preference Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging and purchase intent measurement.
X1.sample: 500 German home cooks (aged 25-55) recruited via a panel, stratified by cooking frequency (daily vs occasional).
X1.measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (EUR). Secondary: open-ended reasons for preference.

prediction_by_theory.T1: At least 30% of participants will indicate purchase intent for the subscription-based combi-steamer within 3 months, and willingness to pay will be above EUR 150 for the subscription model.
prediction_by_theory.T2: At least 25% will indicate purchase intent for the premium-combi-steamer within 3 months, and willingness to pay will be above EUR 200 for the premium model.

X1.decision_rule: If subscription purchase intent >=30% AND subscription willingness to pay >=EUR 150, proceed with a subscription-based home-cook proposition. If premium purchase intent >=25% AND premium willingness to pay >=EUR 200, proceed with a premium-combi-steamer proposition. If neither condition is met, maintain current B2B focus.

revisions.reason: Simulated evidence SYN-D concerns a warehouse label printer and packing errors, which does not address home-cook adoption, subscription willingness to pay, or premium positioning. Therefore it does not affect T1.

final.recommendation: Develop a differentiated subscription-based combi-steamer for home cooks, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing combi-steamer technology and smart‑home integration capabilities. The subscription model provides recurring revenue and aligns with home‑cook convenience needs.
final.target_customer: German home cooks (aged 25‑55) who cook multiple meals daily and value time‑saving automation.
final.value_proposition: A smart, subscription‑based combi‑steamer that learns cooking preferences, sends automated recipes, and updates software, reducing manual effort and decision fatigue.
final.next_action: Run the proposed 12‑week, €20,000 online survey test (500 German home cooks, randomized messaging) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay for subscription vs premium models.
final.uncertainty: The willingness to pay for a recurring subscription fee and the actual demand for automation among home cooks are uncertain. Evidence from public sources does not confirm these assumptions.
would_change_if: If the test shows purchase intent below 30% or willingness to pay below €150 for the subscription model, we would reconsider the subscription approach and explore premium positioning instead.
If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for premium performance and willingness to pay above €200, we would shift focus to a premium-combi-steamer proposition.

arguments.name: Subscription vs Premium Combi-Steamer Preference Test
arguments.method: Online survey with randomized messaging and purchase intent measurement.
arguments.sample: 500 German home cooks (aged 25-55) recruited via a panel, stratified by cooking frequency (daily vs occasional).
arguments.measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (EUR). Secondary: open-ended reasons for preference.

prediction_by_theory.T1: At least 30% of participants will indicate purchase intent for the subscription-based combi-steamer within 3 months, and willingness to pay will be above EUR 150 for the subscription model.
prediction_by_theory.T2: At least 25% will indicate purchase intent for the premium-combi-steamer within 3 months, and willingness to pay will be above EUR 200 for the premium model.

arguments.decision_rule: If subscription purchase intent >=30% AND subscription willingness to pay >=EUR 150, proceed with a subscription-based home-cook proposition. If premium purchase intent >=25% AND premium willingness to pay >=EUR 200, proceed with a premium-combi-steamer proposition. If neither condition is met, maintain current B2B focus.

result.title: Simulated durability-and-repairability proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. Both descriptions showed the same machine, brand, price, warranty, availability, service terms and verified specifications. One emphasized durability and repairability; the other emphasized washing performance and the upfront price. No discount or extra service was added. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 32 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 72 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. A weaker result would not refute a different channel or product theory.

tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. Both descriptions showed the same machine, brand, price, warranty, availability, service terms and verified specifications. One emphasized durability and repairability; the other emphasized washing performance and the upfront price. No discount or extra service was added. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 32 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 72 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. A weaker result would not refute a different channel or product theory.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Electron’x Professional Group investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current professional laundry offering.
constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.

alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home laundry, small businesses, or a new segment).

3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on professional laundry and food‑service equipment.

Participants are recruited from homeowners (n
X1.sample: 300 participants: 150 homeowners (renters and first‑time buyers) and 150 small‑business professionals (gyms, marinas, campsites). Randomly assigned to either exposure group.
X1.measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7‑point Likert scale (1‑not likely, 7‑very likely) and binary intent to purchase within 12 weeks.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Homeowners exposed to consumer‑grade description will show higher average intent than professionals exposed to professional‑grade description, and both groups will be above 5 on the intent scale.

X1.decision_rule: If the average intent for the exposed group is at least 5.5 points higher than the other group, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition for that segment. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 0.5 points, conduct a larger pilot test before committing.

X1.name: Consumer vs Business Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios.
X1.sample: 500 respondents: 250 homeowners/renters and 250 small business owners (hotels, gyms, campsites). Recruit via social media and industry forums.
X1.measure: Willingness to pay (WTP) for a compact self-service machine and intent to purchase based on messaging (convenience vs cost efficiency).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Homeowners will show higher WTP and purchase intent when messaging emphasizes convenience and reduced wait times.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Small businesses will show higher WTP and purchase intent when messaging emphasizes cost savings and labor reduction.

X1.decision_rule: If the average WTP for the convenience message exceeds the average WTP for the cost-efficiency message by at least 10% among homeowners, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on convenience. If the cost-efficiency message outperforms by at least 10% among small businesses, develop a consumer proposition focused on cost savings. If both thresholds are met, pursue both propositions.

revisions.reason: The simulated result (SYN-EPRO-UPDATE) does not address T1, as it tests the effect of durability and repairability messaging on purchase reservations, not consumer demand for convenience. Therefore T1 remains unchanged.

final.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting homeowners and renters, emphasizing convenience and reduced wait times. Begin with a limited pilot in high-homeownership regions to test demand and willingness to pay before scaling.
final.target_customer: Homeowners and renters in urban and suburban areas with limited laundry space and time.
final.value_proposition: Compact, self-service laundry machines that deliver professional-grade performance with a focus on convenience, reducing wait times and effort for daily use.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Business Messaging Test (8 weeks, €15,000) to validate willingness to pay for convenience messaging among homeowners and cost-efficiency messaging among small businesses.
final.uncertainty: The actual willingness to pay for convenience and the size of the consumer market remain uncertain. Evidence shows residential demand exists but does not confirm premium pricing or purchase intent.
would_change_if: If the test shows small businesses prefer cost-efficiency messaging and higher WTP for cost savings, the recommendation would shift to a consumer proposition focused on small businesses.
If homeowners show no premium willingness to pay or low purchase intent, the investment would be reconsidered in favor of no expansion.

result.title: Simulated durability-and-repairability proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. Both descriptions showed the same machine, brand, price, warranty, availability, service terms and verified specifications. One emphasized durability and repairability; the other emphasized washing performance and the upfront price. No discount or extra service was added. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 32 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 72 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. A weaker result would not refute a different channel or product theory.
result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

arguments.reason: The simulated result (SYN-EPRO-UPDATE) does not address T1, as it tests the effect of durability and repairability messaging on purchase reservations, not consumer demand for convenience. Therefore T1 remains unchanged.

arguments.uncertainty: The actual willingness to pay for convenience and the size of the consumer market remain uncertain. Evidence shows residential demand exists but does not confirm premium pricing or purchase intent.
would_change_if: If the test shows small businesses prefer cost-efficiency messaging and higher WTP for cost savings, the recommendation would shift to a consumer proposition focused on small businesses.

Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) space‑constrained home segment (high density housing, small apartments), (2) small business/gym segment (limited staff, high volume), (3) neutral control. Each group sees a product description of a compact consumer‑grade machine (T1) or a durable consumer‑grade machine (T2). The survey measures willingness to pay (WTP) and intent to purchase on a 7‑point scale.
X1.sample: 300 respondents: 100 per segment, recruited via online panels to match demographic distribution of target segments.

prediction_by_theory.T2: Group 2 will show higher average WTP and purchase intent than groups 1 and 3, indicating demand for durable consumer machines.

X1.decision_rule: If the average WTP for the space‑constrained segment (Group 1) exceeds the average WTP for the small business/gym segment (Group 2) by at least 1.5 points on the 7‑point scale, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting homeowners. If the small business/gym segment (Group 2) exceeds Group 1 by at least 1.5 points, develop a proposition for small businesses. If neither segment exceeds the other by the threshold, do not expand into consumer markets.

In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 72 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 32 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. Both descriptions showed the same machine, brand, price, warranty, availability, service terms and verified specifications. One emphasized durability and repairability; the other emphasized washing performance and the upfront price. No discount or extra service was added. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 72 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 32 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Electron’x Professional Group investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current professional laundry offering.
constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.

alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home laundry, small businesses, or a new segment).
2) Expand the existing professional offering into adjacent consumer segments without a differentiated proposition (e.g., add consumer‑focused features to professional models).
3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on professional laundry and food‑service equipment.

Electrolux can reach consumers through existing retail/wholesale channels without major infrastructure changes.
predictions: A test offering a compact self‑service unit in a residential building would achieve at least 10% trial adoption rate within 12 weeks.

X1.name: Segmented Pilot Test: Residential vs Small Business
X1.method: Run a 12‑week pilot in two distinct locations: a residential building (e.g., a multi‑family apartment complex) and a small gym or fitness center. In each location, place a compact self‑service unit at a visible, accessible spot. Track the following metrics: (1) trial adoption rate (number of units used by residents or gym members within 12 weeks); (2) purchase intent measured via a short survey asking about willingness to pay a premium price (e.g., 20% above comparable consumer units); and (3) wholesale sales data (if the unit is sold through a distributor, track units sold).
X1.sample: Residential pilot: 50 units placed in 10 buildings, targeting 2,000 residents. Small business pilot: 20 units placed in 10 gyms, targeting 2,000 gym members.
X1.measure: Trial adoption rate (percentage of units used by residents or gym members within 12 weeks) and purchase intent (percentage of surveyed residents or gym owners indicating intent to purchase at a premium price).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Residential pilot adoption rate ≥ 10% and purchase intent ≥ 20% of surveyed residents; small business pilot adoption rate ≤ 10% and purchase intent ≤ 15% of surveyed gym owners.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Small business pilot adoption rate ≥ 15% and purchase intent ≥ 20% of surveyed gym owners; residential pilot adoption rate ≤ 10% and purchase intent ≤ 15% of surveyed residents.

X1.decision_rule: If the residential pilot meets both adoption threshold (10%) and purchase intent threshold (20%), proceed to develop a differentiated residential proposition. If the small business pilot meets both thresholds, proceed to develop a differentiated small‑business proposition. If neither segment meets its threshold, do not expand into consumer markets.

final.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated residential proposition targeting homeowners and renters with compact, reliable self-service laundry solutions. Begin with a 12‑week pilot in residential buildings to test adoption and purchase intent before scaling.
final.target_customer: Homeowners and renters in multi‑family buildings, student housing, and other residential spaces seeking convenient, cost‑effective laundry options.
final.value_proposition: Electrolux’s professional‑grade reliability and compact design deliver high‑performance self‑service laundry solutions that reduce replacement frequency and fit limited spaces, offering a premium price justified by durability.
final.next_action: Run the proposed 12‑week segmented pilot (residential vs small business) to measure trial adoption and purchase intent. Use the decision rule to decide whether to proceed with a differentiated residential proposition.
final.uncertainty: Consumer willingness to pay a premium price for compact self‑service units is uncertain; the pilot will clarify demand. Additionally, the reach and sales potential through existing retail/wholesale channels remain unknown.
would_change_if: If the pilot shows adoption below 10% or purchase intent below 20% in the residential segment, we would reconsider expansion and focus on small‑business or professional segments.
If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for premium self‑service units, we would reassess the investment case and potentially alter the product positioning or distribution strategy.

arguments.name: Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test
arguments.method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Very unlikely" to 7 "Very likely").
arguments.sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark and Turkey, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Premium messaging or Sustainability messaging.
arguments.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2) for each condition.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Premium messaging will yield a higher average purchase intent score than Sustainability messaging.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Sustainability messaging will yield a higher average purchase intent score than Premium messaging.

arguments.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent score for Premium messaging is at least 1.5 points higher than for Sustainability messaging, proceed with a differentiated premium proposition. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and consider other options.

result.note: Proposed only. Nothing has been run, and its figures are analyst assumptions.

arguments.recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Public evidence does not demonstrate consumer demand for a premium, taste‑focused product. The company is not yet reaching individual buyers, and its financial performance is mixed, with a significant decline in Drinking Water revenue. A differentiated proposition would require a test of willingness to pay and market demand, which is not supported.

result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

X1.name: Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7‑point scale (1‑not interested to 7‑very interested) and to state the top reason for choosing the product.
X1.sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark and Turkey, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Premium Condition (premium taste and purity messaging) or Sustainability Condition (sustainability and plastic waste reduction messaging).
X1.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑not interested to 7‑very interested) and top reason for choosing the product.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Higher purchase intent and sustainability as top reason in Premium Condition compared to Sustainability Condition.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Higher purchase intent and taste and purity as top reason in Sustainability Condition compared to Premium Condition.

X1.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent score in the Premium Condition is at least 1.5 points higher than in the Sustainability Condition, and the difference is statistically significant (p < 0.05), proceed with a premium‑priced differentiated proposition. If the difference is less than 1.5 points or not statistically significant, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and consider other options.

arguments.name: Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test
arguments.method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7‑point scale (1‑not interested to 7‑very interested) and to state the top reason for choosing the product.
arguments.sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark and Turkey, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Premium Condition (premium taste and purity messaging) or Sustainability Condition (sustainability and plastic waste reduction messaging).
arguments.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑not interested to 7‑very interested) and top reason for choosing the product.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Higher purchase intent and sustainability as top reason in Premium Condition compared to Sustainability Condition.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Higher purchase intent and taste and purity as top reason in Sustainability Condition compared to Premium Condition.

arguments.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent score in the Premium Condition is at least 1.5 points higher than in the Sustainability Condition, and the difference is statistically significant (p < 0.05), proceed with a premium‑priced differentiated proposition. If the difference is less than 1.5 points or not statistically significant, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and consider other options.

result.note: Proposed only. Nothing has been run, and its figures are analyst assumptions.

arguments.recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Public evidence does not demonstrate consumer demand for a premium, taste‑and‑purity‑focused differentiated product. The company’s strategic review failure and the lack of consumer‑focused data make it uncertain whether a differentiated proposition would succeed.

result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.
result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

position.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions the product as a premium, health‑focused water purifier emphasizing superior taste and purity. Use premium pricing and direct‑to‑consumer channels to capture higher margins. Conduct a small test (e.g., 300 participants) to validate willingness to pay before full rollout.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Aquaporin A/S investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current water-membrane offering.
constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Evidence must demonstrate demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.
Any recommendation must be based on observable data, not assumptions.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home water purifier for a niche segment).
2) Expand the existing water‑membrane offering to new markets or customer segments without a differentiated proposition (e.g., B2B expansion).
3) No expansion: continue focusing on current B2B membranes and existing distribution channels.
4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct‑to‑consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with retailers) without altering the product proposition.

T1.claim: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home water purifier if they perceive it as a premium, health‑focused product that offers superior taste and purity, leading them to pay a premium price.
T1.who_benefits: Health‑conscious consumers seeking higher purity and better taste in drinking water.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: If consumers shift from viewing water purifiers as a necessity to a lifestyle or health product, they will be willing to purchase a premium‑priced purifier that justifies the cost.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Aquaporin can capture value by pricing the differentiated product at a premium, selling through direct‑to‑consumer channels or premium retailers, and leveraging brand positioning as a premium water‑purification solution.
assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for perceived health and taste benefits.
The premium positioning can be effectively communicated to the target segment.
Distribution channels can reach the premium segment without significant cost.
predictions: In a test offering a premium‑priced differentiated purifier, purchase intent or actual sales will be higher than for a standard‑priced model.
Surveyed consumers will rank taste and purity as top reasons for purchasing the premium product.

T2.how_value_is_captured: Aquaporin can capture value by positioning the product as a sustainable solution, pricing it at a premium for eco‑conscious buyers, and selling through channels that emphasize environmental messaging.
assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for a product that reduces plastic waste.
Environmental messaging can effectively influence purchase decisions.
Distribution channels can highlight sustainability attributes without compromising margins.
predictions: In a test offering a sustainability‑focused differentiated purifier, purchase intent or actual sales will be higher than for a standard‑priced model.

X1.name: Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Very unlikely" to 7 "Very likely").
X1.sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark and Turkey, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions (premium messaging or sustainability messaging).
X1.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2 to 7) for each condition.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Premium messaging will yield a higher average purchase intent score than sustainability messaging.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Sustainability messaging will yield a higher average purchase intent score than premium messaging.

X1.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent score for premium messaging is at least 1.5 points higher than for sustainability messaging, proceed with a premium‑priced differentiated proposition. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, proceed with a sustainability‑focused differentiated proposition. If the difference is less than 0.5 points, no expansion is recommended.

revisions.reason: The simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test (SYN-AQP-UPDATE) does not address consumer perception of premium taste and purity, nor willingness to pay a premium for a differentiated product. It tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under a conditional supply assumption, which is unrelated to T1.

final.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions the product as a premium, health‑focused water purifier emphasizing superior taste and purity. Use premium pricing and direct‑to‑consumer channels to capture higher margins. Conduct a small test (e.g., 300 participants) to validate willingness to pay before full rollout.
final.target_customer: Health‑conscious consumers in Denmark and Turkey who value higher purity and better taste in drinking water.
final.value_proposition: A premium, easy‑to‑use home water purifier that delivers superior taste and purity, justified by a premium price and direct‑to‑consumer distribution.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test (300 participants, 4 weeks, €2,000) to measure purchase intent under each condition.
final.uncertainty: The size of the premium‑priced differentiated market and actual willingness to pay remain uncertain. Evidence from the test will resolve whether T1 or T2 is more supported.
would_change_if: If the test shows a difference of less than 1.5 points between premium and sustainability messaging, indicating no clear preference, the recommendation would shift toward a sustainability‑focused proposition.
If the test shows a difference of less than 0.5 points, indicating no significant difference, no expansion would be recommended.

arguments.name: Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test
arguments.method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Very unlikely" to 7 "Very likely").
arguments.sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark and Turkey, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions (premium messaging or sustainability messaging).
arguments.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2 to 7) for each condition.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Premium messaging will yield a higher average purchase intent score than sustainability messaging.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Sustainability messaging will yield a higher average purchase intent score than premium messaging.

arguments.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent score for premium messaging is at least 1.5 points higher than for sustainability messaging, proceed with a premium‑priced differentiated proposition. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, proceed with a sustainability‑focused differentiated proposition. If the difference is less than 0.5 points, no expansion is recommended.

result.note: Proposed only. Nothing has been run, and its figures are analyst assumptions.

arguments.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions the product as a premium, health‑focused water purifier emphasizing superior taste and purity. Use premium pricing and direct‑to‑consumer channels to capture higher margins. Conduct a small test (e.g., 300 participants) to validate willingness to pay before full rollout.

result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.
result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

arguments.reason: The simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test (SYN-AQP-UPDATE) does not address consumer perception of premium taste and purity, nor willingness to pay a premium for a differentiated product. It tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under a conditional supply assumption, which is unrelated to T1.

arguments.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions the product as a premium, health‑focused water purifier emphasizing superior taste and purity. Use premium pricing and direct‑to‑consumer channels to capture higher margins. Conduct a small test (e.g., 300 participants) to validate willingness to pay before full rollout.
arguments.target_customer: Health‑conscious consumers in Denmark and Turkey who value higher purity and better taste in drinking water.
arguments.value_proposition: A premium, easy‑to‑use home water purifier that delivers superior taste and purity, justified by a premium price and direct‑to‑consumer distribution.
arguments.next_action: Run the proposed Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test (300 participants, 4 weeks, €2,000) to measure purchase intent under each condition.
arguments.uncertainty: The size of the premium‑priced differentiated market and actual willingness to pay remain uncertain. Evidence from the test will resolve whether T1 or T2 is more supported.
would_change_if: If the test shows a difference of less than 1.5 points between premium and sustainability messaging, indicating no clear preference, the recommendation would shift toward a sustainability‑focused proposition.
If the test shows a difference of less than 0.5 points, indicating no significant difference, no expansion would be recommended.

tool_result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

X1.name: Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Very unlikely" to 7 "Very likely").
X1.sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Premium Condition (premium taste and purity messaging) or Sustainability Condition (sustainability messaging).
X1.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2) for each condition.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Premium Condition will yield a higher average purchase intent score than Sustainability Condition.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Sustainability Condition will yield a higher average purchase intent score than Premium Condition.

X1.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent score for Premium Condition is at least 1.5 points higher than for Sustainability Condition, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on premium taste and purity. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and consider other alternatives.

revisions.reason: The simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test (SYN-AQP-UPDATE) does not address consumer perception of premium taste and purity, nor does it provide data on willingness to pay a premium price. Therefore it does not affect the validity of T1.

final.recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Public evidence does not demonstrate consumer willingness to pay a premium price for taste and purity, nor does it provide data on demand for a differentiated product. The company’s strategic review and financial performance also indicate uncertainty about a viable path forward. Continue monitoring market trends and consider a phased approach before
final.target_customer: Health‑conscious consumers seeking higher purity and better taste in drinking water.
final.value_proposition: A differentiated home water purifier positioned as a premium, easy‑to‑use solution that delivers superior taste and purity, sold through direct‑to‑consumer channels or premium retailers.
final.next_action: Conduct a limited pilot test of premium‑priced differentiated purifiers in a specific segment to validate consumer willingness to pay before scaling.
final.uncertainty: Consumer willingness to pay a premium price for taste and purity remains unproven; the company’s financial position and strategic review indicate uncertainty about a viable path forward.
would_change_if: If a pilot test shows purchase intent or actual sales significantly above the threshold of 1.5 points above sustainability messaging, or if new evidence demonstrates strong consumer demand for premium taste and purity.
If the company secures sufficient financing or a strategic partner to support commercialization.

arguments.name: Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test
arguments.method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Very unlikely" to 7 "Very likely").
arguments.sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Premium Condition (premium taste and purity messaging) or Sustainability Condition (sustainability messaging).
arguments.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2) for each condition.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Premium Condition will yield a higher average purchase intent score than Sustainability Condition.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Sustainability Condition will yield a higher average purchase intent score than Premium Condition.

arguments.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent score for Premium Condition is at least 1.5 points higher than for Sustainability Condition, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on premium taste and purity. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and consider other alternatives.

result.note: Proposed only. Nothing has been run, and its figures are analyst assumptions.

result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

X1.name: Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a differentiated home water purifier (e.g., premium taste and purity) and a description emphasizing sustainability and plastic waste reduction. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Not interested" to 7 "Very interested").
X1.sample: 300 adult consumers in Denmark, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Premium Condition (premium taste and purity messaging) or Sustainability Condition (sustainability messaging).
X1.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2 to 7) for each condition.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Premium Condition will yield a mean purchase intent score ≥ 5.5, while Sustainability Condition will yield a mean score ≤ 4.5.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Sustainability Condition will yield a mean purchase intent score ≥ 5.5, while Premium Condition will yield a mean score ≤ 4.5.

X1.decision_rule: If Premium Condition mean ≥ 5.5 and Sustainability Condition mean ≤ 4.5, conclude T1 is supported. If Sustainability Condition mean ≥ 5.5 and Premium Condition mean ≤ 4.5, conclude T2 is supported. If both conditions meet their respective thresholds, both theories are supported. If neither condition meets its threshold, conclude no evidence for either theory.

revisions.reason: The simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test (SYN-AQP-UPDATE) does not address consumer motivations for purchasing a differentiated water purifier, nor does it provide evidence of premium pricing or demand for taste and purity. Therefore it does not affect T1.

final.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes premium taste and purity, targeting health‑conscious consumers willing to pay a premium. Begin with a limited pilot in premium‑priced models and direct‑to‑consumer channels to test demand before broader rollout.
final.target_customer: Health‑conscious consumers in Denmark who currently use standard water purifiers and are willing to pay more for perceived superior taste and purity.
final.value_proposition: A differentiated home water purifier that delivers superior taste and purity, positioned as a premium lifestyle product, justified by clear health benefits and easy maintenance.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Premium vs Sustainability Messaging Test (300 participants, 4 weeks, €2,000) to validate purchase intent under premium and sustainability messaging.
final.uncertainty: The size of the premium‑priced segment and the willingness to pay for taste and purity are unknown. Evidence of strong consumer demand for a differentiated product is limited to company claims and a single simulated test.
would_change_if: If the Premium Condition fails to meet its threshold (mean score < 5.5), the recommendation would shift to a sustainability‑focused proposition or no expansion.
If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for taste and purity at premium prices, the case for T1 would strengthen.

result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

tool_result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

tool_result.title: Simulated maintenance-convenience proposition test
tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.
